records.source: גַּם־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י׀חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: Also these [are the] proverbs of Solomon which [the] men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied.
pieces: These too are proverbs of Solomon, collected and copied by the officials of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

L.1: These also [are] proverbs of Solomon, which [the] men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied.

R.1: Here are more wise sayings of King Solomon. Men who served Hezekiah, king of Judah, copied them down.

decisions.choice: these also are proverbs of Solomon: the heading of a new collection
decisions.reason: The heading opens a second collection of Solomon's sayings (25:1–29:27), after the first one headed at 10:1.

decisions.choice: the men of Hezekiah copied: royal scribes of King Hezekiah
alternatives: moved, transferred (from one collection into another)
decisions.reason: Hezekiah ruled Judah about 715–686 BC, more than two hundred years after Solomon. He restored the temple worship and its songs (2 Kings 18:1–7; 2 Chronicles 29–32; compare 2 Chronicles 29:30). The verb (he'tiqu) means to move or transfer: his court scribes took sayings known as Solomon's and copied them into this collection.

decisions.choice: officials
alternatives: men
decisions.reason: "The men of" a king are his servants at court; in this setting they are scribes.

records.heading: Proverbs copied by Hezekiah's officials

records.source: כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: [It is the] glory of God to conceal a matter, and [the] glory of kings to search out a matter.
pieces: God is honored for keeping things hidden, \q and kings are honored for getting to the bottom of things.

L.2: [It is the] glory of God to conceal a matter, \q and [the] glory of kings to search out a matter.

R.2: God shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness by keeping some things secret. \q A king shows his greatness by finding out the truth about things.

decisions.choice: God's glory is to conceal a matter: his wisdom is beyond full human knowing
decisions.reason: God's ways and works hold more than people can discover (Deuteronomy 29:29; Job 11:7–8; Isaiah 55:8–9).

decisions.choice: the glory of kings is to search out a matter: to investigate before judging
decisions.reason: A king's task was to judge rightly, which requires finding out the facts of a case (1 Kings 3:16–28). The word "search out" links to verse 3.

records.source: שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: [The] heavens for height and [the] earth for depth, and [the] heart of kings, there is no searching.
pieces: As high as the heavens and as deep as the earth, \q so the mind of a king is beyond anyone's probing.

L.3: [As the] heavens for height and [the] earth for depth, \q so [the] heart of kings [is] unsearchable.

R.3: No one can measure how high the sky is or how deep the earth goes. \q In the same way, no one can know all that a king is thinking.

decisions.choice: the heart of kings has no searching: their thoughts cannot be fully known
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind and its plans. Kings search out matters (verse 2), but their own purposes are beyond the reach of their subjects.

decisions.choice: as ... so
alternatives: heavens for height ... and the heart of kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the three items side by side; the comparison is made explicit.

records.source: הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף וַיֵּצֵ֖א לַצֹּרֵ֣ף כֶּֽלִי׃
records.gloss: Remove dross from silver, and there comes out for [the] smith a vessel.
pieces: Take the impurities out of silver, \q and the smith has material for a fine vessel.

L.4: Remove [the] dross from silver, \q and a vessel comes out for the silversmith.

R.4: When impurities are removed from silver, \q a silversmith can make something beautiful from it.

decisions.choice: remove dross from silver: refining by fire
decisions.reason: Silver ore was melted and the dross (slag) skimmed off; only refined metal could be worked (17:3; Isaiah 1:22, 25).

decisions.choice: verses 4 and 5 form one comparison
decisions.reason: The same command, "remove," opens both verses: as dross is taken from silver, so the wicked are taken from the king's presence.

records.source: הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Remove [the] wicked before [the] king, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
pieces: Take the wicked out of the king's presence, \q and his throne will be made secure by justice.

L.5: Remove [the] wicked [from] before [the] king, \q and his throne will be established in righteousness.

R.5: In the same way, remove wicked advisers from around a king. \q Then his rule will be strong because it is fair.

decisions.choice: the wicked before the king: corrupt officials at court
decisions.reason: Those who stand before a king are his advisers and officials; a righteous rule needs righteous servants (16:12; 20:8, 26; 29:12).

decisions.choice: wicked advisers
alternatives: the wicked
decisions.reason: The setting before the king makes clear the wicked are people at his court.

records.source: אַל־תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Do not claim honor before [the] king, and in [the] place of great [people] do not stand.
pieces: Do not promote yourself in the king's presence \q or take your stand among the great,

L.6: Do not put yourself forward before [the] king, \q and do not stand in [the] place of great [people],

R.6: When you are with the king, do not act as if you are important. \q Do not take a place among his great leaders.

decisions.choice: do not claim honor: do not display yourself as important
decisions.reason: The verb (hithhadder) means to make oneself glorious, to put on airs of importance.

decisions.choice: the place of great people: compare Luke 14:8–10
decisions.reason: Jesus' teaching about taking the lowest seat at a wedding feast, so that the host may say "Friend, move up higher," closely follows verses 6–7.

records.source: כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־לְךָ֗ עֲֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: For better [it is that one] say to you, Come up here, than putting you lower before a noble whom your eyes have seen.
pieces: for it is better to be told, "Come up here," \q than to be sent lower in front of a noble \q you have seen with your own eyes.

L.7: for [it is] better [that one] say to you, "Come up here," \q than [that] you be put lower before a noble \q whom your eyes have seen.

R.7: It is better to be invited, "Come up here," \q than to be sent to a lower place in front of important people.

decisions.choice: better to be told to come up than to be put lower: the reason for verse 6
decisions.reason: Taking a high place and being sent down is public shame; waiting to be called up is honor.

decisions.choice: whom your eyes have seen: describes the noble before whom you are shamed
alternatives: what your eyes have seen, do not bring hastily to court (joined to verse 8)
decisions.reason: The verse division keeps the clause with verse 7: the shame happens in front of a noble who saw you take the place. The clause sits awkwardly there, and the Greek and other ancient versions join it to verse 8, as the opening of a warning about rushing into court over what one has seen.

decisions.choice: to be told
alternatives: that one say to you
decisions.reason: The impersonal "one says" is put in the passive.

records.source: אַל־תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר פֶּ֣ן מַה־תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣ רֵעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Do not go out to contest quickly, lest what will you do at its end when your neighbor puts you to shame?
pieces: Do not rush to bring a case to court, \q for what will you do at the end \q if your neighbor proves you wrong and shames you?

L.8: Do not go out quickly to argue [a case], \q for what will you do in the end, \q when your neighbor puts you to shame?

R.8: Do not hurry to take someone to court. \q What will you do if your neighbor proves you wrong and you are embarrassed?

decisions.choice: to contest quickly: to rush into a legal dispute
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is used of quarrels and lawsuits; the warning is against hasty litigation (compare Matthew 5:25).

decisions.choice: lest what will you do: a broken-off warning
decisions.reason: The sentence begins as a warning ("lest") and breaks into a question, as if to say, "or else, what then will you do?"

records.source: רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל־תְּגָֽל׃
records.gloss: Your case argue with your neighbor, and [the] secret of another do not reveal,
pieces: Argue your case with your neighbor directly, \q and do not give away someone else's secret,

L.9: Argue your case with your neighbor [yourself], \q and do not reveal [the] secret of another,

R.9: If you disagree with your neighbor, settle it between the two of you. \q Do not tell other people's secrets to win your argument.

decisions.choice: argue your case with your neighbor: settle it face to face
decisions.reason: Placing "your case" first stresses that it is between the two of you (compare Matthew 18:15).

decisions.choice: do not reveal the secret of another: do not betray a confidence to win the case
decisions.reason: The danger is using what someone told in confidence as ammunition in the dispute (11:13; 20:19).

decisions.choice: to win your argument
decisions.reason: Spells out the setting implied by the first line.

records.source: פֶּֽן־יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: lest he put you to shame, [the one who] hears, and your bad report will not turn back.
pieces: or whoever hears it will shame you, \q and your bad reputation will never go away.

L.10: lest [the one who] hears [it] put you to shame, \q and your bad name not go away.

R.10: If you do, the person who hears it will think badly of you. \q People will never stop talking about what you did.

decisions.choice: your bad report will not turn back: your disgrace will stay with you
decisions.reason: The word (dibbah) is an evil report or slander; here it is the reputation of being someone who betrays confidences.

decisions.choice: [it]
decisions.reason: The object of hearing is the secret of verse 9.

records.source: תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת כָּ֑סֶף דָּ֝בָ֗ר דָּבֻ֥ר עַל־אָפְנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Apples of gold in settings of silver, a word spoken on its times.
pieces: Like golden apples set in silver \q is a word spoken at just the right moment.

L.11: Apples of gold in settings of silver, \q [is] a word spoken at its [right] time.

R.11: Saying the right thing at the right time \q is as beautiful as gold jewelry set in silver.

decisions.choice: apples of gold in settings of silver: a precious, crafted ornament
alternatives: golden fruit carved on a silver background
decisions.reason: The picture is of a costly piece of craftsmanship, perhaps gold fruit set in silver filigree or carved silver. The fruit (tappuah) may be the apple, quince or apricot.

decisions.choice: at its right time: a word that fits the moment
alternatives: on its wheels: in a well-turned, balanced form
decisions.reason: The rare word (ophnaw) is taken as "its times" or "its occasions," a word that suits the moment (15:23). Others connect it with "wheel" and take it as a word well turned, in balanced form, like the two lines of a proverb.

records.source: נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־כָ֑תֶם מוֹכִ֥יחַ חָ֝כָ֗ם עַל־אֹ֥זֶן שֹׁמָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: An earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold, a wise one who reproves on a listening ear.
pieces: A wise person's rebuke, given to an ear that listens, \q is a gold earring, a jewel of the finest gold.

L.12: An earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold, \q [is] a wise reprover to a listening ear.

R.12: When a wise person corrects someone who is willing to listen, \q it is as valuable as fine gold jewelry.

decisions.choice: a wise reprover on a listening ear: correction received well
decisions.reason: The earring hangs on the ear; the wise rebuke is an ornament to the ear that hears it (1:9; 15:31).

records.source: כְּצִנַּת־שֶׁ֨לֶג׀בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר צִ֣יר נֶ֭אֱמָן לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו יָשִֽׁיב׃פ
records.gloss: Like [the] cold of snow on a day of harvest [is] a faithful envoy to those who sent him, and [the] life of his masters he restores.
pieces: Like the coolness of snow in harvest time \q is a reliable messenger to those who send them; \q they refresh the spirit of their masters.

L.13: Like [the] cold of snow in [the] time of harvest \q [is] a faithful messenger to those who send {{gender:them|him}}; \q {{gender:they refresh|he refreshes}} [the] spirit of {{gender:their|his}} masters.

R.13: A messenger you can trust is like a cold drink on a hot day at harvest time. \q That messenger makes the one who sent the message feel refreshed.

decisions.choice: the cold of snow in harvest: welcome refreshment in the heat
decisions.reason: Not a snowfall, which would ruin the crop (26:1), but snow or snow-cooled drink brought down from the mountains, a relief to harvesters in the summer heat.

decisions.choice: restores the life of his masters: revives their spirit
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) is life or inner self; to "restore" it is to refresh (Psalm 19:8; 23:3). A faithful envoy relieves the anxiety of those who sent him (compare 10:26; 13:17).

decisions.choice: a cold drink
alternatives: the cold of snow
decisions.reason: Explains what snow at harvest would mean to a worker.

records.source: נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אָ֑יִן אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: Clouds and wind and rain there is not, a person boasting in a gift of falsehood.
pieces: Like clouds and wind that bring no rain \q is someone who brags about gifts they never give.

L.14: Clouds and wind and no rain, \q [is] a person boasting of a gift [never] given.

R.14: Some people brag about the gifts they will give, but they never give them. \q They are like clouds and wind that bring no rain.

decisions.choice: clouds and wind and no rain: a promise of rain that fails
decisions.reason: In a dry land, gathering clouds and wind raise hopes of rain; when none falls the disappointment is bitter (compare Jude 12).

decisions.choice: boasting in a gift of falsehood: promising a gift that never comes
decisions.reason: A "gift of falsehood" is a false gift: generosity talked about but never delivered.

records.source: בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר־גָּֽרֶם׃
records.gloss: By length of anger a ruler will be persuaded, and a soft tongue will break a bone.
pieces: With patience you can win over a ruler, \q and a gentle tongue can break bone.

L.15: By patience a ruler is persuaded, \q and a soft tongue breaks a bone.

R.15: If you are patient, you can change a ruler's mind. \q Gentle words can break down even the strongest wall.

decisions.choice: length of anger: patience, slowness to anger
decisions.reason: Long of nostrils is slow to anger (14:29; 16:32).

decisions.choice: a soft tongue breaks a bone: gentle speech overcomes hard resistance
decisions.reason: The paradox is deliberate: soft words succeed where force would fail (15:1).

decisions.choice: break down even the strongest wall
alternatives: break a bone
decisions.reason: The picture of breaking bone is turned into a familiar image of overcoming stubborn resistance.

records.source: דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Honey you have found; eat your sufficiency, lest you be sated with it and vomit it.
pieces: If you find honey, eat only what you need, \q or you will have too much and throw it up.

L.16: [If] you have found honey, eat [only] enough for you, \q lest you be filled with it and vomit it.

R.16: If you find honey, eat only as much as you need. \q If you eat too much, you will get sick and throw up.

decisions.choice: honey you have found: wild honey, a good gift to be enjoyed in measure
decisions.reason: Wild honey was a treasured find (Judges 14:8–9; 1 Samuel 14:25–27). Even good things harm when taken to excess; verse 17 applies the same lesson to friendship (compare verse 27).

records.source: הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן־יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Make rare your foot from the house of your neighbor, lest he be sated with you and hate you.
pieces: Do not set foot in your neighbor's house too often, \q or they will get tired of you and come to dislike you.

L.17: Make your foot rare in your neighbor's house, \q lest {{gender:they|he}} grow weary of you and hate you.

R.17: Do not visit your neighbor too often. \q If you do, they will get tired of you and will not want you around.

decisions.choice: make your foot rare: visit seldom
decisions.reason: The verb means to make precious or scarce; visits that are rare stay welcome.

decisions.choice: be sated with you: the same word as in verse 16
decisions.reason: The neighbor can have "too much" of you just as you can have too much honey.

records.source: מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: A war club and a sword and a sharpened arrow, a person testifying against his neighbor [as] a witness of falsehood.
pieces: Anyone who gives false testimony against a neighbor \q is a war club, a sword, a sharpened arrow.

L.18: A club and a sword and a sharp arrow, \q [is] a person who testifies against {{gender:their|his}} neighbor \q [as] a false witness.

R.18: A person who lies about a neighbor in court \q is as dangerous as a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.

decisions.choice: a false witness against a neighbor: the ninth commandment
decisions.reason: The wording echoes Exodus 20:16. False testimony could cost a neighbor property, freedom or life (1 Kings 21:10–13).

decisions.choice: war club: a heavy weapon for shattering
alternatives: hammer
decisions.reason: The word (mephits) comes from a root meaning to shatter or scatter (compare Jeremiah 51:20). The three weapons strike close, at arm's length and from afar.

records.source: שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: A broken tooth and a slipping foot, confidence in [one who] acts treacherously in a day of trouble.
pieces: Like a bad tooth or a lame foot \q is trust in a traitor when trouble comes.

L.19: A broken tooth and a slipping foot, \q [is] confidence in a traitor in [the] day of trouble.

R.19: Trusting someone who is not loyal when you are in trouble \q is like trying to chew with a broken tooth or walk on a twisted foot.

decisions.choice: confidence in a treacherous person in a day of trouble
alternatives: the confidence of a treacherous person (what he relies on)
decisions.reason: Most naturally, it is relying on an unfaithful person: they fail and hurt you just when you need them, like a tooth or foot that gives way under pressure.

records.source: מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד׀בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב־רָֽע׃פ
records.gloss: [One who] takes off a garment on a day of cold, vinegar on soda, and [one who] sings with songs to a sad heart.
pieces: Like taking someone's coat away on a cold day, or like pouring vinegar on soda, \q is singing cheerful songs to a heavy heart.

L.20: [Like one who] takes off a garment on a cold day, [like] vinegar on soda, \q [is one who] sings songs to a heavy heart.

R.20: Singing happy songs to someone who is very sad is like taking away their coat on a cold day. \q It is like pouring vinegar on soda; it only stirs things up.

decisions.choice: vinegar on soda: a reaction that fizzes and spoils
alternatives: vinegar on a wound
decisions.reason: The word (nether) is natron, a natural soda used for washing (Jeremiah 2:22). Vinegar poured on it fizzes and makes it useless. The point is that cheerfulness forced on grief irritates rather than comforts.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text, with three pictures
alternatives: the Greek version: like vinegar on a wound, and like a moth in a garment and a worm in wood, grief harms the heart
decisions.reason: The Greek version reads very differently, with a longer saying about grief that eats away like a moth in clothing. The first line of the Hebrew repeats words from the end of verse 19 and from verse 13, and some think part of it was copied twice. This translation keeps the Hebrew, but the meaning of the verse is uncertain.

decisions.choice: it only stirs things up
decisions.reason: Explains the chemical picture for readers who do not know it.

records.source: אִם־רָעֵ֣ב שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ לָ֑חֶם וְאִם־צָ֝מֵ֗א הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: If [the one who] hates you is hungry, give him bread to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,
pieces: If your enemy is hungry, give them something to eat; \q if they are thirsty, give them water to drink,

L.21: If [the one who] hates you is hungry, give {{gender:them|him}} bread to eat; \q and if {{gender:they are|he is}} thirsty, give {{gender:them|him}} water to drink,

R.21: If someone who hates you is hungry, give them food. \q If they are thirsty, give them water.

decisions.choice: feed the one who hates you: kindness in return for hostility
decisions.reason: The law already required help for an enemy's animal (Exodus 23:4–5), and Proverbs forbids revenge (20:22; 24:17, 29). Paul quotes verses 21–22 in Romans 12:20 (compare Matthew 5:44).

decisions.choice: your enemy
alternatives: the one who hates you
decisions.reason: The participle "one who hates you" is the ordinary way of naming a personal enemy.

records.source: כִּ֤י גֶֽחָלִ֗ים אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: for burning coals you [are] heaping on his head, and YHWH will repay you.
pieces: for you will be heaping burning coals on their head, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will reward you.

L.22: for you will heap burning coals on {{gender:their|his}} head, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will reward you.

R.22: This will make them burn with shame for what they did, and perhaps they will change. \q And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will reward you.

decisions.choice: heap burning coals on his head: bring the enemy to burning shame and remorse
alternatives: an Egyptian rite in which a penitent carried coals on the head as a sign of repentance
heap up God's judgment on the enemy if he stays hostile
decisions.reason: The exact picture is debated. Most often it is taken as the burning shame that undeserved kindness brings, which can lead the enemy to change; an Egyptian text describes a penitent carrying a basin of coals on the head. Others take it as judgment, since coals elsewhere are a picture of punishment (Psalm 140:11). In Romans 12:20–21 the saying serves the call to overcome evil with good, which favors the first sense.

decisions.choice: the LORD will repay you: he rewards the kindness
decisions.reason: Repayment is left to the LORD (20:22; 19:17).

decisions.choice: burn with shame for what they did, and perhaps they will change
alternatives: heap burning coals on their head
decisions.reason: The image is explained in the sense chosen above; the hope of change is part of that sense.

records.source: ר֣וּחַ צָ֭פוֹן תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם וּפָנִ֥ים נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים לְשׁ֣וֹן סָֽתֶר׃
records.gloss: A wind of north brings forth rain, and faces indignant, a tongue of secrecy.
pieces: As a north wind brings rain, \q so a gossiping tongue brings angry looks.

L.23: A north wind brings forth rain, \q and a secret tongue, angry faces.

R.23: A north wind brings rain. \q In the same way, gossip brings angry faces.

decisions.choice: a north wind brings forth rain: a sure cause and effect
alternatives: the north wind holds back rain
decisions.reason: In Israel rain usually comes with west winds off the sea, and the north wind is cold. "North" may mean northwest, or the saying may come from a region where north winds bring storms. Some take the verb as "is in labor with" or "holds back." The point is clear either way: as the wind brings rain, a secret tongue brings anger.

decisions.choice: a tongue of secrecy: slander spoken behind someone's back
decisions.reason: Talk done in secret (Psalm 101:5) produces open anger when it comes to light.

records.source: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: Better to dwell on a corner of a roof than a woman of contentions and a house of sharing.
pieces: It is better to live up in a corner of the rooftop \q than to share a home with a wife who quarrels.

L.24: [It is] better to live on a corner of [the] roof \q than [with] a woman of quarrels in a shared house.

R.24: It is better to live alone in a corner of a flat roof \q than to share a house with a wife who is always arguing.

decisions.choice: of contentions, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: of strife (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written consonants and the scribes' reading differ only in the form of the word for quarrels; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the same saying as 21:9
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 21:9 almost word for word; 21:19 and 27:15 make the same point. A flat roof could hold a small room or shelter, cramped and exposed to the weather.

records.source: מַ֣יִם קָ֭רִים עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: Water cool on a weary soul, and a report good from a land of distance.
pieces: Like cold water to someone worn out and thirsty \q is good news from far away.

L.25: [Like] cool water to a weary soul, \q [so is] good news from a distant land.

R.25: Good news from a faraway place \q is like cold water when you are tired and thirsty.

decisions.choice: good news from a far country: news long awaited
decisions.reason: With slow travel, news from far off was rare and often anxiously awaited (compare Genesis 45:25–28).

decisions.choice: a weary soul: a person faint with thirst
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) can mean throat or person; a weary soul is someone parched and exhausted (Psalm 63:2).

records.source: מַעְיָ֣ן נִ֭רְפָּשׂ וּמָק֣וֹר מָשְׁחָ֑ת צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־רָשָֽׁע׃
records.gloss: A spring fouled and a fountain ruined, a righteous [person] giving way before a wicked [person].
pieces: When the righteous give way before the wicked, \q it is a trampled spring, a fouled well.

L.26: A muddied spring and a polluted fountain, \q [is] a righteous [person who] gives way before [the] wicked.

R.26: When a good person gives in to an evil person, \q it is like a spring of clean water that has been made dirty.

decisions.choice: a righteous person who gives way before the wicked
alternatives: a righteous person who falls before the wicked
decisions.reason: The verb (mat) means to totter or slip. Whether by yielding to pressure or by being brought down, the righteous person ceases to be a clean source of life for others (10:11; Ezekiel 34:18–19).

records.source: אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: To eat honey much [is] not good, and the searching of their honor [is] honor.
pieces: Eating honey to excess does no good, \q and seeking honor for yourself brings no honor.

L.27: To eat much honey [is] not good, \q and searching out their glory [is] glory.

R.27: Eating too much honey is not good for you. \q In the same way, it is not good to try to make yourself look important.

decisions.choice: too much honey: as in verse 16
decisions.reason: Good things become harmful in excess.

decisions.choice: seeking one's own honor is not honor
alternatives: searching out weighty matters is honor
to search out their honor is honor (the Hebrew as it stands)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads literally "searching their honor, honor," which is obscure. Many take the "not" of the first line to carry over: just as too much honey is not good, seeking honor for oneself is not honorable (compare 27:2). Others change the vowels or letters to read "to search out difficult things is honor," echoing verse 2, or "to be sparing of weighty words." This translation gives the first sense, but the meaning is uncertain.

decisions.choice: searching out their glory [is] glory
decisions.reason: The Literal level keeps the Hebrew as it stands, without the carried-over "not."

records.source: עִ֣יר פְּ֭רוּצָה אֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֑ה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A city broken into, there is no wall, a person who there is not restraint for his spirit.
pieces: Someone without self-control \q is a city breached, left with no walls.

L.28: [Like] a city broken into [and] without a wall, \q [is] a person who has no control over {{gender:their|his}} spirit.

R.28: A person who cannot control their temper or desires is like a city with broken walls. \q Anything can get in and do harm.

decisions.choice: a city broken into without a wall: defenseless
decisions.reason: A city's walls were its protection; once breached, it lay open to any enemy (Nehemiah 1:3).

decisions.choice: no restraint over his spirit: no self-control
decisions.reason: The spirit here is temper and impulse; compare 16:32, where ruling one's spirit is better than taking a city.

decisions.choice: Anything can get in and do harm
decisions.reason: Explains what a wall-less city meant.
